rows.short_description: Escalation.ps1 positional binding let a missing dash on -Comment silently corrupt -RunId/-Decision instead of erroring clearly
rows.comment:
Root cause: Escalation.ps1 used default [CmdletBinding()] positional binding across all 16 params. A missing leading '-' before -Comment (e.g. `...-State in-progress comment "long text"`) caused PowerShell to silently bind the bare token 'comment' to -RunId (position 2, first unbound) and the actual comment text to -Decision (position 3), which then failed ValidateSet with a confusing error pointing at -Decision -- nothing about the real problem (missing dash on -Comment) or that -RunId got corrupted too.

Separately: because the error was a PS parameter-binding terminating error thrown before the script ever called into iba.app.lib.escalation, it never reached the escalation DB -- no mechanism exists (or is expected, per cfg_behaviour_rule terminal class review) to auto-capture a PS-side terminating error as an escalation row; the researcher has to report it in chat, as happened here.

Fix applied: added PositionalBinding=$false to Escalation.ps1's CmdletBinding. Verified: (1) the exact failing command now throws a clear "A positional parameter cannot be found that accepts argument 'comment'." pointing at the actual bad token, instead of corrupting -Decision; (2) normal named-parameter usage (-Action History -Id 753) still works unchanged; (3) grepped all iba/app/ps/*.ps1 callers -- every existing invocation of Escalation.ps1 uses named parameters only, none rely on positional args, so no caller is broken; (4) re-ran the researcher's original -Action Update -Id 753 command with -Comment corrected -- landed clean as v2.

rows.short_description: content_index is ~63%+ of iba.db's 7.5GB from generated analysis files never added to cfg_content_index_exclude -- same failure mode fixed once already (2026-08-17), recurred bigger
rows.comment:
Investigated at the researcher's request ("why is iba.db 7.8GB"). Numbers, not estimates -- full table scans / GROUP BYs run live against iba.db:

DB itself: 7.5GB, page_count=1,968,156 x page_size=4096. freelist_count=0 -- this is real data, not reclaimable bloat (a VACUUM would not shrink it).

One table dominates by far: content_index, 14,118,338 rows -- 14x the next-biggest table (verse_lexical, 960,064 rows). Raw text payload alone (measured via full LENGTH() scan) averages 262 bytes/row = ~3.45GB before its 3 indexes (1 implicit unique + 2 explicit, one on the file_path TEXT column) are counted -- plausibly the large majority of the 7.5GB.

Root cause, with precedent: this is the SAME failure mode the researcher already hit and partially fixed once. cfg_content_index_exclude has exactly one row, added 2026-08-17: "exclude programme prose from content_index -- generated analysis prose saturated with the very biblical vocabulary being indexed (one file alone produced ~597,000 hits)." Confirmed that fix still holds (0 rows from that path today) -- but the SAME pattern has since recurred, much bigger, from folders never added to the exclude list:

- iba/app/verse-analysis/**/*.md (303 files, the per-book verse-lexical extracts built 2026-08-09): 4,487,358 rows -- 31.8% of the whole table on its own. Individual files run 130k-210k rows each (e.g. luke-1-24-verse-lexical-v1-20260809.md alone: 210,781 rows).
- Sessions/Session_Clusters/** (e.g. wa-cluster-M15-grouped-v1-20260511.md: 193,865 rows from ONE file): 4,460,980 rows -- another 31.6%.

Together these two folders alone are ~63% of content_index's 14.1M rows (~8.95M), on top of the 76% of all rows (10.7M) that are key_type=gloss -- and the highest-frequency gloss values indexed are ordinary English words that happen to coincide with Strong's glosses (sense: 152,430 lines; word: 101,985; which: 71,830; step: 71,680; group: 77,603; first: 56,674; both: 51,097 -- not the Hebrew/Greek-conjunction stoplist contentindex.py already has, which only covers 1-word matching for actual particles like and/or/not/this/that/with).

Not fixed here -- raising for your decision, not acting unilaterally: whether to add iba/app/verse-analysis/ and Sessions/Session_Clusters/ to cfg_content_index_exclude (same mechanism as the 2026-08-17 fix), and/or widen the gloss stoplist beyond conjunctions to cover generic high-frequency English words -- either changes what content_index can actually find, which is your call, not mine to make silently. ContentIndex-SizeProfile.ps1 already exists for exactly this kind of pre-decision review (built 2026-08-17, same session as the first fix) -- worth running before deciding scope.
